extmeta.ImageDescription: Fragment of a glazed tile recycled in the outside of the South wall of the chancel of St John's Priory. All that's left of the maker's mark is "Browne &". It might be Browne & Co. in Bridgwater, according to this website: https://www.brocross.com/Bricks/Penmorfa/Pages/england4b-4.htm, but the repairworks on St John's in 1817 are slightly early to be using Browne & Co bricks which were only patented in 1827[1].
